title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A_0 is an abelian variety over a field k of characteristic p>0. The previous page belongs to a section on deformations of ordinary Barsotti–Tate groups, titled 'determination of the canonical stratifications on the deformations'.

Question. For infinitesimal deformations A/Λ of A_0, with Λ a local artinian k-algebra, when can one attach a k-stratification to H = H^1_DR(A/Λ), naturally in A and compatibly with base change? A k-stratification here means a descent datum ('rectification') u: p_1^*H ≅ p_2^*H over Spf(Λ ⊗̂_k Λ) satisfying the cocycle condition. In characteristic 0 the Gauss–Manin connection would supply this. In characteristic p it gives only a connection, or a stratification over PD-neighbourhoods. A full stratification over Λ⊗Λ is a much stronger requirement.

Necessary condition. Let M be the formal moduli of A_0 over k and A_M the universal deformation. Then H = DR^1(A_M/M) would need a formal stratification compatible with F: H^{(p)} → H and V: H → H^{(p)}. So the geometric isomorphism type of (H_x, F_x, V_x) would be constant over the points x of M, equal to that of (H_0, F_0, V_0). Since the generic fibre of the universal deformation is ordinary, this 'surely' forces A_0 to be ordinary.

Ordinarity is expressed via the Hodge exact sequence 0 → H^{10} → H → H^{01} → 0 and its Frobenius twist. One has Im V = Ker F = (H^{10})^{(p)} and Ker V = Im F. Ordinarity says the p-th power (Hasse–Witt) map on t_{A_0^*} = H^1(A_0, O) = H^{01} is bijective, i.e. it induces an isomorphism (H^{01})^{(p)} ≅ H^{01}.

Ordinarity is open, so the same holds for any deformation A/Λ. Then Im F = F(H^{(p)}) maps isomorphically onto H^{01}. Hence the extension H of H^{01} by H^{10} is canonically split by Im F. This is the conjugate (Frobenius) filtration being transverse to the Hodge filtration, i.e. the unit-root splitting.

The next page continues. Im F is stable under any F-compatible rectification. Only (H^{10})^{(p)} = Ker F is a priori stable, not H^{10} itself: from u(F_1)^{(p)} = F_2^{(p)} one cannot deduce u(F_1) = F_2 unless the base is formally smooth, where Frobenius is a monomorphism. This is the beginning of constructing the canonical (Serre–Tate-type) stratification on deformations of ordinary abelian varieties / BT groups.
errors: The relations Im V = Ker F = (H^{10})^{(p)} and Ker V = Im F hold for any abelian variety (exactness of the Dieudonné / de Rham structure). They are not what characterises ordinarity. The ordinary condition is the transversality Im F ∩ H^{10} = 0, i.e. Im F ≅ H^{01}, equivalently bijective Hasse–Witt. Grothendieck states this correctly a few lines later, but the displayed diagram presents the general relations as if they defined ordinarity.

The step 'constant type of (H_x,F_x,V_x) implies A_0 ordinary' is marked 'sans doute'. It is correct, since the ordinary locus is dense in the formal moduli (non-vanishing Hasse invariant generically), but no proof is given on this page.

The page is silent on uniqueness of the stratification. In the ordinary case, a stratification built from the Serre–Tate splitting into étale and multiplicative parts does preserve H^{10}. So the next page's worry about H^{10} concerns what can be deduced from F-compatibility alone, not a genuine obstruction.

ideas.what: Asking for a full k-stratification (hyperstratification), not merely a connection, on H^1_DR of infinitesimal deformations in char p, functorial and base-change compatible.
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius-compatible stratification / crystal structure relative to k; p-curvature and higher obstructions of the Gauss–Manin connection
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (IHES notes 1966/68) treats stratifications generally; this specific question is not known to be published by him

ideas.what: Existence of an F,V-compatible stratification on the universal deformation forces constant F,V-type, hence ordinarity of A_0.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / isotriviality of Newton–Hodge type for horizontal F-structures; ordinary locus dense
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz ('Serre–Tate local moduli', 1981; Dwork–Katz unit-root theory); Norman–Oort for density

ideas.what: Ordinarity as bijectivity of the p-th power (Hasse–Witt) on H^1(A,O), equivalently Im F maps isomorphically onto H^{01}.
In the ordinary case Im F (conjugate filtration) gives a canonical splitting of the Hodge filtration of H^1_DR over any deformation base.
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root splitting; transversality of conjugate and Hodge filtrations (Deligne–Illusie/Katz); Serre–Tate canonical splitting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (1973 'p-adic properties of modular schemes', 1981), Deligne, Serre–Tate

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks to characterise exactly when deformations admit canonical F-compatible stratifications of de Rham cohomology. He obtains ordinarity as a necessary condition and begins to show sufficiency, giving an intrinsic de-Rham/Frobenius approach to Serre–Tate canonical coordinates that predates Katz's 1981 treatment. The idea is well known now; the novelty is only historical priority and the framing via full stratifications rather than connections.
missed.quote: quand est-il possible, sur les déf. inf. A/Λ de A_0 ... d'associer une k-stratification sur DR^1(A/Λ), compatible avec changement de base et fonctorielle en A ? ... Cela implique sans doute que A_0 est "ordinaire"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that by 1969 Grothendieck had linked full (Frobenius-compatible) stratifications in char p to ordinarity and to the canonical splitting by Im F. This bears on the history of Serre–Tate coordinates, unit-root crystals and Frobenius-constant structures.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear, early formulation of 'canonical stratification exists ⇒ ordinary ⇒ conjugate filtration splits Hodge'. The mathematics is now standard (Serre–Tate, Katz, Deligne), so the interest is mainly historical priority and the stratification viewpoint, not new results.
transcription_corrections: 'variété[?] des modules formels' is likely 'la variété des modules formels' (formal moduli of A_0); acceptable.
'le rel.[?] max.[?] de V[?] d'ordre p_1[?]' is uncertain; plausibly 'i.e. le rang maximum de V (ou F) ...' expressing maximal rank of Frobenius/Verschiebung, i.e. p-rank g. The image is hard to read.
'Mais dans ce cas pour la A sur Λ' should likely read 'Mais dans ce cas, pour toute A sur Λ, il en est de même dans DR^1(A)'.

The last lines likely read: 'Cela implique que l'ext. H = DR^1(A) de H^{01} par H^{10} [est] canoniquement scindée, car Im F = F(H^{(p)}) est un [sous-module] tel que Im F → H^{01} [iso] évidemment'. The written '= H^{01}' with an arrow suggests 'Im F ≅ H^{01}'.
